subject: Reasoning
topic: Statement and Assumptions — Implicit Reasoning (W10 B2)

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The school has announced additional coaching classes for students appearing in board examinations.'
Assumption I: Board examinations are important for students' futures.
Assumption II: Additional coaching will help students perform better in board exams.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both assumptions underlie the announcement. Assumption I: without recognising board exams as important, there is no reason to provide special coaching — so I is necessary for the statement to make sense. Assumption II: the school wouldn't announce extra classes unless it believed they would improve performance — so II is also implicit. Trap: choosing only II misses the fundamental premise in I.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Please carry an umbrella if you go out today.'
Assumption I: There is a possibility of rain today.
Assumption II: The person being advised owns an umbrella.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: without the possibility of rain, advising someone to carry an umbrella makes no sense. Assumption II is NOT implicit: the advice to carry an umbrella does not presuppose the person already owns one — they might be told to buy one. The statement is about precaution against rain, not about existing ownership of an umbrella.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'In case of fire, use stairs — do not use the elevator.'
Assumption I: The elevator may be unsafe to use during a fire.
Assumption II: People normally prefer to use the elevator over stairs.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the specific warning against using the elevator in fire presupposes that it is dangerous in such situations (electrical failure, entrapment). Assumption II is also implicit: you would only need to specify 'do not use the elevator' if people would otherwise be inclined to do so. If everyone naturally chose stairs, the warning would be unnecessary.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Wanted: experienced software engineers for leading MNC.'
Assumption I: Experienced software engineers are available in the job market.
Assumption II: The MNC requires software engineering expertise for its operations.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I: placing an advertisement presupposes that qualified candidates exist in the market — otherwise advertising would be pointless. Assumption II: no company advertises for a skill set it doesn't need — the need for software engineering expertise is the very reason for the advertisement.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Only persons with proven integrity should be appointed to senior government positions.'
Assumption I: Some candidates for senior positions may lack integrity.
Assumption II: Integrity is the single most important quality for senior government roles.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: you would not need to specify 'only persons with integrity' if all candidates already had it. The qualifier 'only' implies that some do not. Assumption II is NOT implicit: the statement prioritises integrity but does not claim it is the SINGLE most important quality — other qualities (competence, experience) may also matter. 'Should be appointed' does not imply a singular criterion.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Lending money to friends is like losing a friend.'
Assumption I: Friends sometimes fail to repay borrowed money.
Assumption II: Money is valued more highly than friendship.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the statement implies that lending creates conflict because friends don't repay — this is the mechanism by which a friend can be 'lost'. Assumption II is NOT implicit: the statement warns that lending RISKS friendship (i.e., friendship is valued), which is the opposite of saying money is more important. Trap: students may infer II from a misread of the proverb.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Companies should invest in training fresh graduates rather than exclusively hiring experienced professionals.'
Assumption I: Training fresh graduates may be more cost-effective or beneficial than hiring experienced staff.
Assumption II: Experienced professionals always demand higher salaries than fresh graduates.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the recommendation to train fresh graduates over hiring experienced staff presupposes that this approach offers some advantage (cost, loyalty, customisation of skills). Assumption II is NOT implicit: the statement does not specify WHY experienced professionals are not preferred — it could be cost, cultural fit, or other factors. 'Always demand higher salaries' is too absolute an assumption not stated in the original.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has decided to impose a heavy tax on luxury goods.'
Assumption I: People will continue to buy luxury goods even after the tax.
Assumption II: Imposing a tax on luxury goods will generate additional revenue.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption II is obviously implicit: no government would impose a tax unless it expected revenue. Assumption I is also implicit but subtler: if the government expected everyone to stop buying luxury goods after the tax, revenue would be zero — so it implicitly assumes demand will persist. Trap: choosing only II misses the demand-side assumption in I.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The bridge over the river has been declared unsafe; please do not cross it.'
Assumption I: People may attempt to cross the bridge.
Assumption II: There is an alternative route available to cross the river.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit: warning people not to cross presupposes they might otherwise attempt it — without this, the warning is unnecessary. Assumption II is NOT implicit: the warning simply prohibits crossing — it says nothing about the availability of alternative routes. The absence of an alternative does not contradict the statement; it just makes the situation more difficult.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Reading quality newspapers every day makes one a better-informed citizen.'
Assumption I: Quality newspapers provide accurate and reliable information.
Assumption II: Being better-informed is desirable for citizens.

Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit: the statement only makes sense if quality newspapers actually provide reliable information that informs readers. Assumption II is implicit: the statement is a recommendation ('makes one a better-informed citizen' is presented positively), which only holds if being better-informed is considered desirable. Without II, the statement would have no motivating value.
